summary: The vocabulary and Pfam domain databases operate at fundamentally different resolutions. The vocabulary provides sub-domain annotation at ~4 amino acid granularity, yielding 12.6x more annotations per protein than Pfam. The vocabulary covers 326 proteins (16.3% of sample) that have zero Pfam domain annotations, demonstrating that it captures sequence structure that established domain databases do not resolve.

resolution.interpretation: The vocabulary provides 12.6x finer resolution than Pfam. Each protein is annotated with ~18 vocabulary tokens vs ~1.4 Pfam domains. Vocabulary tokens average ~4 amino acid equivalents, operating at sub-domain scale.

functional_discrimination.interpretation: The vocabulary assigns functional departments to 168 proteins that have zero Pfam domain annotations, covering 22 functional categories. This demonstrates that the vocabulary captures functional information at a resolution that Pfam domain annotation does not reach.
